```sql
WITH agg AS (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           count(DISTINCT o.id)     AS order_count,
           sum(ol.quantity)         AS quantity,
           sum(ol.line_total_cents) AS revenue_cents,
           count(DISTINCT pv.id)    AS variant_count
      FROM order_lines ol
      JOIN orders o            ON o.id = ol.order_id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
     GROUP BY pv.product_id
     ORDER BY quantity DESC, revenue_cents DESC
     LIMIT %(limit)s
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       a.order_count,
       a.quantity,
       a.revenue_cents,
       a.variant_count
  FROM agg a
  JOIN products p ON p.id = a.product_id
 ORDER BY a.quantity DESC, a.revenue_cents DESC
```

Er wordt nu per `product_id` geaggregeerd en gelimiteerd vóór de join met `products`. Daardoor hoeft er niet op vijf (brede) tekstkolommen gegroepeerd te worden en wordt `products` alleen voor de top-N opgezocht. De join blijft gelijkwaardig dankzij de FK `product_variants.product_id → products.id`, en de uiteindelijke ORDER BY blijft behouden.
